description: docs/external/rule-sets.md:95 says any query reaching for anything else is refused before it runs; unlisted columns instead fail in MySQL with unknown-column. Line 119 says so correctly.

docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md:64 claims guard-internal refusals redact to REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR; RlsError ones get REDACTED_RLS / REDACTED_RELATION because redacted_refusal_text checks RlsError first. Checklist VC-21 agrees.
Startup catalog check in preflight opens with connect_timeout only, no read/write timeout like the request-time check; a stalled server hangs serve and validate --check-db.
Frozen rule-set records keep mutable list fields; LoadedRuleSets.rule_set returns the live RuleSet.
TableRule.row_rule: Any = None declares a field whose only valid state is absent.
RuleSetSelection does not validate its own fields (positive user_id, bound account).
CatalogConfirmation.confirmed is a public writable bool beside its lock.

docs/external/rule-sets.md:85 says the `rule-set key missing` refusal means the rule-set field is absent or empty; a request whose _meta holds more than 64 keys also gets this refusal (_request_metadata(ctx, count_declared_keys=True) returns {}), so an operator sending a valid key in a large _meta gets no explanation.
